column1: What's the critical difference between a key with a value versus a key without a value in YAML, and how does this affect GitHub Actions workflow structure?
column2:
Key with value: name: "My Workflow"
  • The key gets a direct value (string, number, boolean)
  • Cannot have child keys - YAML will throw an error
  • Used for final values like workflow names, commands
Key without value: name:
  • Creates a parent object that can contain child keys
  • Must be followed by indented child properties
  • Used for complex objects like jobs, steps
GitHub Actions impact:
jobs: (no value - allows child job definitions)
  build: (no value - job object)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest (has value - cannot have children)
    steps: (no value - allows step array)

column1: What are YAML's two array syntax formats and when should you use each in GitHub Actions?
column2:
Block format (multi-line):
steps:
  - name: Checkout
    uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - name: Test
    run: npm test

Inline format (square brackets):
os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
branches: [main, develop]
types: [opened, closed, synchronize]

When to use each:
  • Block format: Complex objects with multiple properties (steps, jobs)
  • Inline format: Simple lists of primitive values (strings, numbers)
  • Both are standard YAML - not GitHub Actions-specific syntax

column1: What are the three main categories of workflow events in GitHub Actions and provide one key example for each?
column2:
1. Repository-level events - push, pull_request, issues, release
  2. Manual triggers - workflow_dispatch (UI button), API calls
  3. Scheduled triggers - schedule with cron expressions (minimum every 5 minutes)

column1: What's the difference between an event type and an activity type in GitHub Actions, and how do they work together?
column2:
Event type = The broad category of what happened
  • Examples: pull_request, issues, release
Activity type = The specific action within that event
  • pull_request activities: opened, closed, synchronized, reopened
  • issues activities: opened, closed, labeled, assigned
  • release activities: published, created, deleted
How they work together:
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize] (Only these activities)
  issues:
    types: [opened, labeled] (Not all issue activities)

Why this matters: Fine-grained control - run workflows only for specific activities, not every event occurrence.

column1: What are the GitHub-specific requirements and limitations for cron expressions in scheduled workflows?
column2:
Requirements:
  • 5 elements only: minute hour day_of_month month day_of_week
  • Standard cron syntax with asterisks for "all"
GitHub limitations:
  • Minimum frequency: Every 5 minutes (*/5 * * * *)
  • No every-minute execution - not supported
  • Initial delay: First run may take 15+ minutes
Common patterns:
schedule:
  - cron: "0 0 * * *" (Daily at midnight)
  - cron: "0 9 * * 1" (Monday at 9 AM)
  - cron: "*/5 * * * *" (Every 5 minutes - testing only)

column1: How do you enable manual workflow execution and access trigger information within the workflow?
column2:
Enable manual trigger:
on:
  workflow_dispatch: (Adds "Run workflow" button in UI)

Access trigger information:
steps:
  - name: Show trigger
    run: echo "Triggered by ${{ github.event_name }}"

Available context:
  • github.event_name - Event that triggered workflow
  • github.actor - User who triggered the workflow
  • github.ref - Branch/tag reference
UI capabilities: Branch selection, immediate execution, visible in history as "manually run"

column1: What's the recommended trigger management strategy during workflow development vs. production?
column2:
During active development:
on: push (Auto-trigger for testing)

After completion:
on: workflow_dispatch (Manual control only)

Benefits:
  • Prevents spam in Actions tab
  • Focuses attention on workflows being developed
  • Saves resources and improves organization
Testing strategy:
  1. Use push during development
  2. Test workflow_dispatch with UI button
  3. Create test branch for pull_request events
  4. Remove schedule after testing to avoid continuous runs
  5. Clean up test branches and PRs

column1: How can you create sophisticated event filtering for complex CI/CD pipelines?
column2:
Branch and activity filtering:
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
    branches: [main, develop]
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['src/**', 'tests/**']
  release:
    types: [published]

Multiple trigger combinations:
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 2 * * *" (Nightly builds)

Why this flexibility matters:
  • Precise automation - trigger exactly when needed
  • Resource efficiency - avoid unnecessary workflow runs
  • Complex pipelines - different actions for different scenarios
  • Integration capabilities - enables sophisticated CI/CD workflows
